**Pathway Analysis Narrative**

The differential metabolite profile is most strongly associated with **Tyrosine Metabolism (KEGG map00350)**, which achieved a highly significant enrichment (FDR = 0.0, fold-enrichment = 435) and captured five of the nine input compounds. Additional disease-associated pathways — including **Alkaptonuria**, **Dopamine Beta-Hydroxylase Deficiency**, and **Monoamine Oxidase-A Deficiency** — were also significantly enriched, sharing an overlapping set of metabolites with the primary pathway.

The key driver compounds in the primary pathway are **3,4-Dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (C04043)** and **5,6-Dihydroxyindole (C05578)**. Membership queries confirmed both metabolites are annotated in KEGG map00350 (Tyrosine metabolism). C04043 also participates in dopamine-related disease pathways (Dopamine Beta-Hydroxylase Deficiency) and the **Disulfiram Action Pathway**. **Pyrocatechol (C15571)** and **Dihydrobiopterin (C02953)** further support the involvement of aromatic amino acid and pterin cofactor networks. **Copper (C00070)** is confirmed in tyrosine metabolism but is not connected via a direct KEGG reaction path to 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde within the search depth, indicating that it likely acts as a cofactor rather than a precursor in this dataset.

The matched disease pathways (Alkaptonuria, Dopamine Beta-Hydroxylase Deficiency, Monoamine Oxidase-A Deficiency) collectively implicate disruption of aromatic amino acid catabolism and monoamine neurotransmitter processing. Eicosapentaenoic acid may contribute anti-inflammatory context given its interaction with membrane lipid mediators.

**Limitations:** Pathway membership data did not confirm direct reaction relationships among all listed metabolites within the search depth. The biological interpretation is anchored to the verified pathway names and disease associations returned by RaMP; no additional biological claims are made beyond those directly supported by the enrichment results.
